we present an approach to reasoning about actions on multi-agent temporal Kripke structures and provide a number of results about the properties preserved under these actions.

we have developed a novel framework for reasoning about actions in temporal Kripke structures, we have studied its properties, we have provided axiomatizations for the resulting theories, and we have connected our framework with the literature on time in DEL.

the question of what can be done with the temporal structure of a multi-agent Kripka model by means of action model-induced operations.

the question of how the “objective” time structure and agents’ epistemic states can be modified by informational actions, and how the effects of such modifications can be formally described and analyzed.

the question how to reason about the effect of actions on temporal Kripkes models, in a way that allows the actions to modify not only the epistemic structure, but also the temporal structure of these models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our approach provides a natural and elegant way to extend action model-style operations to temporal Kripkemodels in a manner that is both faithful to the original DEL approach and that allows actions to affect the temporal structure of a Kripke model.
we present an extension to DEL that allows us to reason about actions on temporal models, and we provide an analysis of the resulting logic.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach is a natural way of extending action model-style operations on temporal Kripkes models, which allows us to study the effects of informational actions on the flow of time.
we have provided a framework for studying the interplay of time, knowledge, and action in a uniform manner.

we present a general framework that can be used for reasoning about a variety of informational operations that modify the structure of temporal models, and we study the preservation of a number of important epistemics and temporal properties under such operations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
temporal action model-based operations can be used to model a wide range of temporal and epistemic actions, including the actions of agents and the actions of the environment.
temporal action models provide a natural way to model and reason about informational actions that can control the temporal structure of the world.
the action models framework can be fruitfully extended to temporal Kripkes models in a way that is consistent with the existing literature.
